# Contributing

Notes for people working on Babqua itself. If you're here to *use*
Babqua, start with [Getting Started](getting-started.qmd) instead.

## Repo layout

- `_extensions/bb/` — **source of truth** for the published
  extension. The Lua filter (`babqua.lua`), bb-side runtime
  (`runtime.bb`), lifecycle scripts (`babqua-lifecycle.bb`,
  `babqua-nrepl-client.bb`), stylesheet (`babqua.css`), and the
  Quarto metadata (`_extension.yml`) all live here.
- `docs/` — this Quarto book. Each chapter is a `.qmd` file; the
  filter renders the live `{.clojure .bb}` blocks against the
  in-tree extension.
- `docs/_extensions/bb/` — symlink shim pointing back to
  `_extensions/bb/`. Quarto requires an `_extensions/` directory
  adjacent to the `_quarto.yml` it's rendering, so the docs book
  needs its own copy of the extension. The symlinks let the docs
  pick up changes to the in-tree extension immediately, without
  going through `quarto add`. **If you add a new file to
  `_extensions/bb/`, mirror it as a symlink in
  `docs/_extensions/bb/`.**
- `dev-notes/` — design notes, gotchas, review personas, backlog.
  Not part of the rendered book; not user-facing.

The published install path is `_extensions/scicloj/bb/` (created by
`quarto add scicloj/babqua`), one level deeper than the in-tree
`_extensions/bb/`. Both layouts work because Quarto resolves a
filter named `bb` by searching either form.

## Local setup

```bash
git clone https://github.com/scicloj/babqua
cd babqua/docs
quarto render
```

The symlinks are committed, so there's no setup script. A clean
render produces `docs/_book/` with one HTML file per chapter.

For a faster iteration loop while editing a single chapter:

```bash
cd docs && quarto render demo.qmd
```

`demo.qmd` exercises every Kindly kind plus stdout, errors, and a
live HTTP fetch — a good single-file smoke test.

## Where to look

| Question | File |
|:---|:---|
| Why does Babqua exist as a sibling to Janqua? What's the v1 cut? | `dev-notes/babqua-design.md` |
| What's queued up but not yet done? | `dev-notes/backlog.md` |
| Lua / Pandoc / Quarto gotchas the filter steps around | `dev-notes/lua-filter-gotchas.md` |
| Sharing a runtime contract across dialects (Babqua / Janqua / future) | `dev-notes/multi-dialect-design.md` |
| Versioning, release process, and what goes in a tag | `dev-notes/versioning-releases.md` |
| Review angles to inhabit when reading the code | `dev-notes/review-personas/` |
| End-to-end flow of a single render | [How It Works](how-it-works.qmd) |

## Memory and dev-notes

Per-project Claude Code memory lives at
`~/.claude/projects/-workspace-Dropbox-projects-daslu-babqua/memory/`.
The CLAUDE.md at the repo root is the entry point for any AI assistant
working on the codebase — it points at the design doc, the persona
files, and the memory directory.

## Releases

The `/release` skill walks through the steps; the underlying
checklist lives in `dev-notes/versioning-releases.md`. Each release
is gated on running the persona reviews in
`dev-notes/review-personas/` — a fresh pass derisks the install path
before the tag goes public.
